answer: An agent economy resists sybil attack by requiring costly, repeated proof-of-work that consumes real resources, like the copper wiring of a physical network. Each identity must perform verifiable labor across multiple epochs, so spinning up thousands of sock puppets becomes as expensive as paying for each connection. A new entrant is a narrow inlet into the system: it gains influence only gradually, verified by peers, never all at once. Cheap identities fail because attestation history itself is the currency of trust, and forging it costs more than a sonnet of computation.
